This tutorial introduces to data augmentation with the package `housepi`. 
We'll walk through the process of associating augmented variable to individuals to then proceed with standard model generation and inference.
We start by loading the package:

```{r}
library(housepi)
```

The commands to generate and build a model are the same used for all models presented so far. 
As an example, we use the default model "augm_onset_single_intr", where survey conditioned on single introduction follows the times of onset:

```{r}
# generate the model
hemi <- generate_model("augm_onset_single_intr")

# associate data, parameters and setup
build_model(hemi, 
            data = "data/data.csv", 
            params = "data/params-ex2.csv",
            setup = "data/setup-ex2.csv")

# store the choice of the parameters used in the simulations
params <- hemi$params()
```

## Build with Augmented Variables

Loading the augmented variable definitions is more delicate, since in principle their configurations could depend on data and/or parameter.

**augmented:** a DataFrame (or a file) with the augmented variables, the respective models and proposer rules needed for the Bayesian Monte Carlo.


```{r}
# associate augmented variable definitions
build_model(hemi, augm = "data/augm.csv")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(read.csv("data/augm.csv"))
```

## Simulate an Augmented Model

We run a simulation with the usual method `simulate`. 

```{r}
# override status of the dataset according to simulation 
hemi$simulate()

# load the simulated dataset
df <- hemi$data()
# show the results of the simulation 
head(df[c("status", "incub_period", "onset_date")])
```
We can see that in addition to the status, the simulation also associates the values of the augmented variables: the incubation period and the onset time.

As a sanity check, we can verify that inference returns the parameters used for the simulation.

```{r}
mcmc_trace <- run_inference(hemi)

# visualize the trace of the MCMC chain
coda::traceplot(mcmc_trace)

# store the results
results <- summary(mcmc_trace)

# collect the information for the check
inames <- params[params["infer"] == TRUE, "name"]
data.frame(Expec = params[params["infer"] == TRUE, "value"],
           Mean = results[["statistics"]][inames, "Mean"],
           Q2.5 = results[["quantiles"]][inames, "2.5%"],
           Q97.5 = results[["quantiles"]][inames, "97.5%"])
```
